entries.topic: Medical bankruptcy: two estimates

claims.text: Himmelstein et al. (AJPH, 2019), surveying 910 bankruptcy filers in 2013-16, reported that 66.5% cited medical issues (bills or illness-related income loss) as contributing to their bankruptcy; the figure counts contribution as reported by filers, not causation.

Dobkin, Finkelstein, Kluender and Notowidigdo (NEJM, 2018), linking hospital records to credit and bankruptcy records, estimated that hospitalisations cause about 4% of bankruptcies among non-elderly adults, and argued that survey shares overstate causation because they count bills that would not by themselves have led to bankruptcy.

entries.topic: Childcare costs and Israel daycare subsidy

claims.text: OECD definition: net childcare cost = out-of-pocket cost of full-time centre-based care for two children aged 2 and 3, after childcare benefits, tax reliefs and benefit changes; the standard couple earns 100% + 67% of average earnings. The OECD PF3.4 text places the US among countries where net cost for this couple is at least 18% of average earnings (2021); no exact Israel figure is legible in the document (Israel data year 2020).

United States, 2022 (OECD data, reported by Statista): a couple with two young children, both working full-time at the average wage, spends 20% of disposable household income on childcare; a single parent on the average wage spends 37%.

Israel: no OECD net-childcare-cost value (as % of average wage or household net income) could be retrieved from an accessible source; the OECD Data Explorer requires JavaScript and the direct SDMX query was not reachable. Not estimated.

Israel daycare subsidy (age 0-3, state-supervised daycare centres): both parents must work or study; eligibility and subsidy level are set by per-capita household income and household size. Average monthly subsidy about NIS 2,300 (Haredi families), NIS 1,600 (Arab), NIS 1,500 (non-Haredi Jewish). In 2022, 89,250 households (103,981 children) used supervised centres; about 226,000 households with children 0-3 met the work/study test and about 140,000 also met the income test. Annual cost about NIS 1.2 billion. Most children in daycare are in private daycare not covered by the scheme.

Israel daycare subsidy is run through certified centres supervised by the Ministry of Labor's daycare division; the work test is 24 hours a week for both parents; only about half of eligible mothers received the subsidy in 2018.

entries.topic: Child support enforcement and guaranteed maintenance

claims.text: Israel: under the Maintenance (Assurance of Payment) Law (in force since 1972), a resident woman holding an unpaid court maintenance judgment is paid monthly by the National Insurance Institute, which then collects from the debtor. The payment is the lower of the court award or the regulation amount (equal to the income-support rate for single-parent families); if NII collects more than it paid, the difference goes to the woman.

Israel 2023: monthly average 11,564 women received NII maintenance payments (12,436 in 2022, -7.0%); NII paid NIS 318.1 million in 2023 and collected NIS 309.1 million from debtors (collections include debts relating to past as well as current recipients, so the two are not a like-for-like recovery rate); average monthly payment NIS 2,204 in Dec 2023 (about 18.6% of the average wage).

United States FY2024 (preliminary): the IV-D child support program collected 65% of current support due; total distributed collections $29.5 billion (IV-D and non-IV-D); 12.2 million children served; 87% of cases had orders; 63% of cases with arrears had a collection.

United States FY2024: about $26.7 billion distributed ($25.8 billion paid to families); 65.3% of current support collected; more than 11.6 million cases; $115.7 billion of the $146.7 billion owed was past-due, of which $7.5 billion was paid.

United States, Census CPS Child Support Supplement, 2017 data: of 5.4 million custodial parents due support, 45.9% received the full amount, 24.0% partial, 30.2% none; $30.0 billion due, $18.6 billion (62.2%) received. The Census published a 2022-data report (P60-285, Aug 2025), but its full-receipt percentage could not be extracted.

No US public guarantor exists equivalent to Israel's NII advance: US agencies enforce and collect but do not pay the custodial parent when the payer defaults (inference from program structure, not a single-source statement).

entries.topic: Paid sick leave

claims.text: Israel: under the Sick Pay Law (1976) every employee accrues 1.5 paid sick days per full month worked (18 a year), up to a cap of 90 days; accrual is automatic and days cannot normally be cashed out.
Israel pay scale: day 1 of illness unpaid, days 2-3 at 50% of wages, day 4 onward 100%; full pay from day 1 for certain serious conditions (e.g. cancer treatment, dialysis).

United States, March 2026 (BLS NCS): 81% of private industry workers had access to paid sick leave; full-time 88%, part-time 59%. A March 2025 all-private figure was not extracted.

claims.text: OECD net replacement rate (net household income in unemployment as % of disposable income before job loss), initial phase (2nd month), single person no children, no social assistance or housing benefit, 2025: previously earning 67% of the average wage, Israel 65%, US 55%; previously earning 100% AW, Israel 59%, US 38%. entries.topic: Corporate and top personal tax rates, incentives and effective rates: Israel vs US

claims.text: Statutory corporate income tax: Israel 23% (2025 and 2026, PwC); US 21% federal, combined federal and average state statutory rate 25.57% (Tax Foundation 2025; OECD unweighted average 24.20%, worldwide average 23.58% across 181 jurisdictions).

Israel's incentive regimes under the Law for the Encouragement of Capital Investments (PwC, June 2026): Preferred Enterprise 7.5% in Development Area A / 16% elsewhere; Special Preferred Enterprise 5% / 8% (for ten years); Preferred Technology Enterprise 7.5% / 12% on qualifying income; Special Preferred Technology Enterprise 6%. Dividends from PTE/SPTE to foreign parent companies (90%+ foreign-held) withheld at 4%, otherwise 20%.

Intel Kiryat Gat deal (announced 26 Dec 2023): Israeli government grant $3.2bn, 12.8% of a planned $25bn investment in Fab 38; Intel committed to buy NIS 60bn (about $16.6bn) from Israeli suppliers over a decade; Finance Ministry official said Intel's corporate tax rate rose from 5% to 7.5% under the deal. ITEP (Feb 2024): 342 consistently profitable large US corporations paid an average effective federal income tax rate of 14.1% over 2018-2022 (statutory 21%); 109 paid zero federal income tax in at least one year; total tax breaks $275bn.
Israel State Comptroller (Nov 2022): estimated tax benefits (tax expenditures) NIS 67bn in 2019, up 34% from 2015. A more recent Tax Authority total (2023-2025) was not found.

entries.topic: Non-US official aid to Israel (German naval subsidies) and private philanthropic inflows

claims.text: German subsidies for Israel's Dolphin submarines (AFP/UPI 2012): the first two Dolphins were donated by Germany (the UPI account ties this to the 1953 reparations agreement; other accounts link it to the 1991 Gulf War - not resolved here); Germany paid half of the roughly $700m cost of the third; it agreed to pay one-third of the $1.27bn cost of the fourth and fifth (ordered 2006); for the sixth (signed March 2012, about $659m) Germany covered up to EUR 135m, described as about a third.

AP (30 Nov 2011): Germany set aside EUR 135m ($180m) in its budget to pay about a third of another Dolphin submarine; of Israel's three Dolphins at the time, two were entirely funded and one half-funded by Berlin.

Sa'ar 6 corvettes (ordered May 2015): four ships from ThyssenKrupp for about NIS 1.8bn (about EUR 430m / $480m); German government contribution EUR 115m per AFP; Ynet reported Germany would subsidise one third.

Dakar-class submarines (agreement Jan 2022): three submarines from ThyssenKrupp for about EUR 3bn ($3.4bn); German government contribution EUR 540m under a 2017 bilateral agreement (about 18%, book's arithmetic).

No authoritative total of non-US official (state) aid to Israel was found; no other state military grant programme comparable to US FMF was found in this pass. Israel is not an OECD DAC ODA recipient in current data (not separately verified here).

Private philanthropy: donations to Israeli nonprofits totalled $4.4bn in 2015 (all sources, per CBS), of which $2.8bn (about two-thirds) came from abroad (Tel Aviv University Institute for Law and Philanthropy); US funders: 1,179 organisations gave $1.8bn in 2015 (centralised bodies $707m, 'friends of' groups $752m, family foundations $87m); evangelical Christian groups under 3% of foreign donations. 2015 is the latest comprehensive year cited; no newer authoritative annual total found.

entries.topic: US foreign assistance totals and military share; host-nation support received by the US

claims.text: US foreign assistance disbursements (ForeignAssistance.gov, per Pew, constant 2025 dollars): FY2023 $85.1bn; FY2024 $73.5bn (category table gives $71.6bn); FY2025 $47.3bn; FY2026 through 1 July 2026 $7.0bn. Aid was 0.67% of federal spending in FY2025 (about 1% for most of FY2008-FY2021).

Military/security share: the 'peace and security' category was $18.2bn in FY2024 (about 25% of the $71.6bn total, book's arithmetic) and $7.3bn in FY2025, 15.5% of FY2025 aid, the smallest share since FY2001. Pew's figures are disbursements; an obligations total for FY2024/FY2025 was not retrieved (ForeignAssistance.gov home page not reachable in this session).

Israel in FY2025: $3.31bn disbursed (Pew), 99.8% military; USAFacts gives about $3.3bn obligated in FY2025, all military, ranking first among 43 high-income recipients; Pew says Israel's FY2025 figure was down 51.4% from FY2024. Ukraine FY2025 $6.70bn (84.9% non-military).

Host-nation support is a different category from foreign aid: Japan pays for part of the cost of stationing US forces in Japan under a Special Measures Agreement - JPY 1,055.1bn (about $8.6bn at 2022 rates) over five years to March 2027 (about JPY 210bn a year, book's arithmetic); talks on the next agreement began in mid-2026.

No source found that states in terms that the US receives foreign military aid; the US is a donor, and no foreign grant programme to the US comparable to FMF was found. The 'receives none' point rests on absence of evidence, not a direct citation.

entries.topic: Three Families: US BLS CE 2024 by income quintile (1, 3, 4)

claims.text: BLS CE 2024 is the latest calendar-year release (published 19 Dec 2025, delayed from the usual September; no 2025 calendar-year tables were listed on bls.gov/cex/tables.htm as of 21 Oct 2026). Quintiles are of consumer units ranked by income before taxes; 135,760 thousand consumer units in all. Quintile lower bounds: 2nd $29,932, 3rd $57,452, 4th $94,511, top $155,925.

BLS CE 2024: INCOME AFTER TAXES WAS NOT PUBLISHED for 2024 (BLS: the tax model provider did not update its model). Latest published after-tax incomes are 2023: all consumer units $87,869; third quintile $66,606; fourth quintile $104,559 (FRED shows no 2024 observation).

BLS CE 2024 income before taxes (mean, USD/year per consumer unit): all $104,207; lowest quintile $16,658 (2023: $15,596); third quintile $74,474 (2023: $71,057); fourth quintile $121,548 (2023: $116,717). Changes agree with BLS Report Table 5 (+$1,062, +$3,417, +$4,831).
BLS CE 2024 average annual expenditures (USD per consumer unit): all $78,535; lowest quintile $35,046; second $50,054; third $66,900; fourth $89,972; highest $150,342 (Table C).

BLS CE 2024 housing (USD/yr): all $26,266; lowest quintile $14,563; third $24,093; fourth $29,374. Shelter: all $16,317; lowest $9,178; third $15,257; fourth $17,851. Definitions (BLS CE glossary, not re-read for this entry): CE housing = shelter + utilities + household operations + housekeeping supplies + furnishings; owners' shelter is actual outlays (mortgage interest, property tax, maintenance, insurance), NOT imputed rent; mortgage principal is excluded (counted as asset change).

BLS CE 2024 food (USD/yr, food at home + away; alcohol separate): all $10,169; lowest quintile $5,498; third $9,097; fourth: NOT RETRIEVED (FRED CXUFOODTOTLLB0105M under maintenance; BLS xlsx not reachable).
BLS CE 2024 transportation (USD/yr): all $13,318; third quintile $11,657; fourth $15,952; lowest quintile: NOT RETRIEVED (BLS Report Table 5 gives only its 2023-24 change, +$188, +3.8%).
BLS CE 2024 healthcare (USD/yr; out-of-pocket incl. health insurance premiums paid by the household, excl. employer-paid): all $6,197; lowest quintile $3,445; third $5,676; fourth $7,247.

BLS CE 2024 education (USD/yr): all $1,569; lowest quintile $828; third $749; fourth $1,353. Caveat: FRED's 2023 values (727, 1,079, 1,176) do not match the 2023-24 changes in BLS Report Table 5 (+$113, -$232, +$250), though the 2024 levels are consistent with Table 5 within ~$2.

BLS CE 2024 personal insurance and pensions (life insurance + Social Security and pension contributions; included in CE 'average annual expenditures'): all $9,797; lowest quintile $711; third $6,248; fourth $11,934.

BLS CE 2024 average number of persons per consumer unit: all 2.4. By quintile: NOT RETRIEVED (published in the BLS quintile xlsx, which could not be read; no FRED series located). Number of consumer units in lowest quintile: 27,139 thousand.

entries.topic: Three Families: Israel CBS HES 2024/2023 by income decile/quintile

claims.text: Israel CBS Household Expenditure Survey 2024 (released ~13 Oct 2026) is the latest. National averages per household per month: gross money income NIS 27,173 (2023: 26,330); net money income NIS 22,555 (2023: 21,606); total consumption expenditure incl. imputed housing services NIS 18,695; money expenditure excl. imputed housing NIS 15,370; median gross income NIS 20,540; Gini 0.333 (2023: 0.349). Housing 25%, transport and communications 18.4%, food 17.9% of consumption.

CBS HES 2024 by decile of households ranked by net money income per standard person (NIS/household/month, as tabulated by Davar): net money income D1 7,276; D2 10,598; D3 13,513; D4 16,160; D5 18,565; D6 21,241; D7 25,310; D8 29,046; D9 34,286; D10 49,496. Expenditure D1 11,902; D2 11,174; D3 12,317; D4 13,647; D5 15,094; D6 15,477; D7 15,992; D8 17,173; D9 19,106; D10 21,800. Check: the decile means average to 22,549 (≈ net income 22,555) and 15,368 (≈ money expenditure 15,370), so the expenditure column is MONEY expenditure excluding imputed housing services, not total consumption (18,695).

CBS quintile tables for HES 2024 (or 2023) were NOT reached; published quintile values not found in any accessible source. Derived from the decile table (CBS deciles each hold 10% of households, so a quintile mean = simple mean of its two deciles, rounding aside): net money income Q1 ≈ NIS 8,937, Q3 ≈ 19,903, Q4 ≈ 27,178; money expenditure (excl. imputed rent) Q1 ≈ 11,538, Q3 ≈ 15,286, Q4 ≈ 16,583 per household per month, 2024. These are book arithmetic, not CBS-published figures.

CBS HES 2024 bottom vs top decile: household size bottom decile 4.1 persons (Calcalist) or 3.9 (Bizportal; sources disagree), top decile 2.6 (Calcalist) or 2.7 (Bizportal); earners 0.9/0.8 vs 1.8/1.9; work share of income 60.9% vs 81%; home ownership 35.5% vs 79.5% (national 62.5%); renting 56.5% vs 18.3% (national 32.7%); average rent NIS 3,924. Gross money income, household size and category spending by quintile/decile for 2024 were not found.

CBS HES 2023 (press release 1 Jan 2026), Table A, by decile of net money income per standard person: persons per household all 3.2, bottom decile 4.2, 4th decile 3.1, 7th decile 3.0, top decile 2.4; earners 1.5 / 0.9 / 1.4 / 1.6 / 1.7. National: gross money income NIS 26,330, net 21,606, consumption incl. imputed housing 18,088, money expenditure 14,823. Definitions: consumption includes imputed housing services for owner-occupied/rent-free/key-money dwellings valued at the rent of similar dwellings in the same locality; 'food' in the headline share (17.9%) INCLUDES fruit and vegetables; 2023 income is not comparable with earlier years (methodology change).

Category spending by quintile (closest published proxy, NOT the HES table): CBS's Feb 2025 CPI-weights update (HES 2022-2023 data in 2024 prices) gives total monthly consumption per household: average NIS 19,319.89, bottom quintile 13,765.34, top quintile 25,848.33. Shares of consumption, bottom / middle (Q3) / top quintile: food EXCL. fruit and veg 19.8% / 16.0% / 13.2%; transport and communications 15.4% / 19.2% / ~20%; housing (incl. imputed owner-occupied housing services) 21.6% / 24.9% / ~28%. Bottom vs top only: education services 7.1% vs 4.5%; private medical services 2% vs 4%; rent 10% vs 5%. Fourth-quintile values and Q3 NIS total not given.

entries.topic: Life satisfaction by income, US and Israel

claims.text: United States, Gallup Mood of the Nation (phone, 2-15 Jan 2025, n=1,005): share 'very satisfied' with the way things are going in their personal life, by annual household income: under $40,000 38%; $40,000-$99,999 42%; $100,000+ 55% (2020: 54%, 66%, 76%). Total satisfied (very + somewhat), all adults: 81%. Income-group totals for very+somewhat not published. Verbatim question in the topline, not reproduced in the article.

Gallup's US life-evaluation measure (Cantril ladder, 0-10): 'On which step of the ladder would you say you personally feel you stand at this time?' and 'about five years from now'; thriving = current 7+ and future 8+. Gallup states life evaluation rises with income across the full distribution, but no recent thriving-by-income percentages were found in accessible releases.

Israel CBS (Social Survey, released for Rosh Hashanah, Sep 2026): 92.2% of Israelis aged 20+ satisfied with their lives (Jews 92.6%, Arabs 90.6%); 70.2% satisfied with their financial situation. CBS Social Survey 2023: 91.1% satisfied. Question wording not given in these sources; the CBS Social Survey item is believed to be 'In general, are you satisfied with your life?' on a 4-point scale, with 'satisfied' = very satisfied + satisfied (NOT VERIFIED against a CBS questionnaire).

Israel life satisfaction by income quintile from the CBS Social Survey: NOT FOUND in any accessible CBS release or press coverage (CBS tables not reachable). Not estimated. No cross-country survey giving both countries by income group was found (Gallup International 2024 reports income breakdowns only as a 37-country aggregate).
